title: Consent-aware rate-limited audit proxy (PRD draft)
content:
Purpose
---
This is a working PRD sketch for a small-footprint audit-proxy that sits at the customer-managed edge (or on-prem adaptor) and emits compact, consent-aware audit bundles to Redwood. The goal is to provide sufficient forensic evidence for operator actions and network changes while respecting customer privacy/consent constraints and avoiding high-volume telemetry spikes (rate-limited).

Why this exists (problem statement)
---
Customer-managed networking introduces two opposing needs: (1) Redwood needs reliable, auditable evidence to support change approvals and incident investigations (for Private customers under contract), and (2) customers want to limit what telemetry leaves their environment for IP/data protection and cost reasons. Current onboarding relies on full syslog or large packet captures which are noisy and expensive. We need a compact, signed evidence format plus a local proxy that enforces sampling, consent policies, and per-tenant rate limits before forwarding.

Goals (measurable)
---
- Provide a compact audit bundle (< 15KB typical) per change event that contains: event header, signed metadata, delta snapshot (diff), optional flow-summaries, and a proof-hash linking to locally stored artifacts.
- Support configurable local sampling: 100% for high-risk changes, 1-5% for routine heartbeats; default policy defined by operator tiers.
- Enforce consent rules: operator-controlled allowlist/blocklist fields, SLO to redact payloads within 100ms of capture when consent denies forwarding.
- Soft-rate-limit forwarding to Redwood control plane: default 10 bundles/min per customer (configurable), with burst capacity and backpressure semantics.
- Attach cryptographic attestation (ed25519 sig or AWS KMS HSM reference) to each bundle to preserve non-repudiation.
- Integrate with Console rollouts: show "evidence arrival rate" and sampling-level in per-customer dashboards.

Non-goals
---
- This proxy will not attempt to be a full SIEM or replace customer observability stacks.
- It is not the long-term archival store; Redwood will index and keep compact records for query SLO only—full archives stay customer-side or in retained artifact stores.
- Not handling deep packet payloads (no PII extraction); only metadata and diffs.

User stories
---
- As a platform engineer at AcmeCorp (customer), I can set an approval policy that marks "router config change" events as high-risk so 100% of these bundles are forwarded.
- As a Redwood SRE, I can query per-customer evidence arrival and know whether sampling was applied for the window when an incident occurred.
- As a compliance reviewer, I can request a signed evidence pack for a specific change and verify the attestation chain.

High-level design
---
1) Local audit-proxy (binary/docker/arm) runs in customer environment (edge VM or operator container). It hooks into customer change sources: mgmt-plane webhooks, syslog change lines, operator CLI wrappers, or network config push events.
2) Proxy constructs a Compact Evidence Bundle (CEB): header (ts, event-id, source), metadata (user, ticket id, pre/post diffs), flow-summary (optional), policy-eval snapshot (sampling decision + reason), and signature.
3) Policy engine: local YAML with policies (sampling rates, allowlists, redact rules). Can be patched via signed manifest from customer admin (so operators can temporarily increase sampling during incidents).
4) Rate limiting and delivery: proxy maintains token-bucket per-tenant with backpressure to avoid cloud-tier overload. When limits reached, low-priority bundles are queued to local store and a 1-line summary is sent (title + proof-hash).

Compact Evidence Bundle (CEB) fields (draft)
---
- version: string (v1)
- event_id: UUID
- timestamp: ISO8601
- actor: (string) operator id / service
- ticket: optional string (JIRA/Confluence/Inc)
- change_diff: compact unified diff (pref) or key-value deltas
- flow_summary: list of {src,dst,proto,bytes,time-window} (optional)
- policy_decision: sampling:true/false, policy_id, reason
- consent_flags: user-acknowledged:true/false, allowed_tags:list
- proof_hash: base64(sha256(artifact))
- signature: base64(ed25519(signature over bundle))

Policy examples
---
- router-config-change: sampling=1.0, rate-limit=30/min, priority=high
- routine-heartbeat: sampling=0.02, rate-limit=10/min, priority=low
- emergency-mode (manual): override sampling=1.0 for 15m window via signed manifest

Delivery semantics and failure modes
---
- Normal: push HTTPS to Redwood ingress using client cert or mTLS. Bundles queued if transient errors.
- Rate-limited: low-priority bundles are stored locally and a compact index entry (event_id + proof_hash + reason) is forwarded instead.
- Offline: proxy enters offline mode, retains bundles encrypted on-disk up to retention cap; operator CLI to extract and upload later.
- Corruption/verification failure: Redwood rejects invalid signature; retain and flag on customer console + notify operator.

Security & privacy considerations
---
- Default redaction: IPs in flow_summary are hash-prefixed (allow partial matching but not full content) unless customer policy allows full IP.
- Consent model: customers must select one of: {allow-full, consent-by-operator, redact-by-default}. Consent manifests are signed by customer admin.
- Key management: allow local KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) integration OR built-in ed25519 keypair generated at install. Support HSM/KMS attestation exchange for enterprise customers.
- Data minimization: no payload-level extraction; only diffs and flow summaries.

Console / UX surface
---
- In Console: per-customer -> Evidence tab: shows sampling rate, rate-limit state, last bundle arrival, queue depth, attestation health.
- Alerting: when sampling prevents required evidence (e.g., policy mismatch) send a warning to customer admin and Redwood account owner.
- On-demand fetch: operators can request a "pull pack" which instructs the proxy to upload specific stored bundles (e.g., for a non-sampled time range). Pull must be approved by customer admin (signed request).

SLA and cost model
---
- Redwood will guarantee ingestion SLO of 99% for high-priority bundles if within configured rate-limits.
- Storage: Redwood stores only indexed CEBs and proof-hashes for 90 days by default. Long-term archival is a separate contract.
- Pricing: base per-customer ingestion allowance (e.g., 1,000 bundles/month) + overage per-bundle. Need finance input.

Rollout plan (MVP -> Beta -> GA)
---
MVP (Q1): basic proxy, CEB v1, local policies, default sampling, Redwood ingest + verification, Console evidence list.
Beta (Q2): KMS integration, signed manifests, sampling override UI, basic backpressure metrics.
GA (Q3): HSM attestation, retention contracts, per-route sampling presets, audit-query API.

Open questions / Risks
---
- Bandwidth tradeoffs: what are acceptable default size goals for CEBs across typical customer change patterns? Need corpus.
- Legal: need privacy review for partial IP hashing and whether hashed IP counts as PII in certain jurisdictions.
- Ops: how do we safely rotate proxy keypairs without breaking existing proof chains?

Next steps / action items
---
- Data team: collect sample change events from three pilots to size CEB (INF-4023). (Miguel)
- Security & Legal: privacy signoff on IP hashing and consent model. (Samira)
- Engineering: prototype proxy that intercepts a mock config push and emits a signed CEB to dev ingest endpoint. (Jared)
- Product: finalize default policy presets and pricing guidance. (Priya)

Notes to self / rough ideas
---
- Consider differential evidence: instead of full diffs, keep lightweight checkpoints and reference deltas by proof-hash to reduce upload frequency.
- Could integrate with Optimize to suggest sampling levels based on historical incident frequency (automated risk scoring).
